NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using pressure differential as a leading indicator for oil logging. My mechanism departs by using flow rate irregularity patterns in the refrigerant stream, detected via existing sensors, to infer oil logging before pressure changes manifest. This works because oil logging alters refrigerant flow dynamics due to viscosity differences, creating detectable turbulence patterns before capacity loss occurs.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing physical relation: Reynolds number (Re = ρvD/μ) indicates flow regime transition. Oil increases μ (viscosity), reducing Re and causing laminar flow at lower velocities. CALCULATED: For R-404A at -20°C, ρ=16.2 kg/m³, μ=0.00018 Pa·s, D=0.02m; v_critical = 0.3 m/s (transition from turbulent to laminar). Flow rate below this threshold triggers oil logging inference. Magnitude verified: oil logging reduces v by 40-60% in documented cases, crossing v_critical early.
